subject: English
text: What did Lencho write on the envelope of the letter containing his request for money?
explanation: Lencho wrote 'To God' on the envelope, placed the letter inside, and went to town to post it.

subject: English
text: How many deputy presidents were sworn in during the South African democratic inauguration ceremony?
explanation: Two deputy presidents were sworn in: Mr. de Klerk as second deputy president, and Thabo Mbeki as first deputy president.

subject: English
text: In 'A Triumph of Surgery', what did Mrs. Pumphrey mistakenly believe Tricki was suffering from?
explanation: Mrs. Pumphrey thought Tricki was listless because he lacked energy, so she assumed he was suffering from malnutrition and began overfeeding him.

subject: English
text: In Robert Frost's poem 'Fire and Ice', what does the element of 'Ice' symbolize?
explanation: Ice symbolizes hatred, coldness of heart, rigidity, and indifference among human beings.

subject: English
text: In 'The Thief's Story', what educational skills did Anil teach Hari Singh?
explanation: Anil taught Hari Singh how to write his name, promised to teach him to write whole sentences, and to add numbers.

options.text: Writing his name, writing whole sentences, and adding numbers.
Reading newspapers and writing business letters.
Speaking English fluently and public speaking.

subject: English
text: Fill in the blank with the correct determiner: He has ________ knowledge on the subject, which is why he failed the test.
explanation: 'Little' has a negative meaning, implying almost none, which fits the context of failing a test due to lack of knowledge.

subject: English
text: What was the title of the first essay Anne Frank was assigned by Mr. Keesing as a punishment?
explanation: As a punishment for talking in class, Mr. Keesing assigned her an essay titled 'A Chatterbox'.

options.text: Quack, Quack, Quack, said Mistress Chatterbox

subject: English
text: In 'His First Flight', how did the mother seagull trick the young seagull into flying?
explanation: She flew close to him with a piece of fish in her beak but halted just out of his reach, prompting him to dive for the food in hunger.

options.text: She stood near him with food and stopped just out of his reach, forcing him to dive.
She pushed him off the ledge when he was not looking.
She pretended to be attacked by a larger bird.
She flew away with all his siblings, leaving him alone.

subject: English
text: In 'A Tiger in the Zoo', why does the tiger ignore the visitors walking past his cage?
explanation: The tiger feels restricted and helpless behind the bars, realizing that his strength is locked up and the visitors pose no interest or threat to him.

options.text: Because he is helpless and his strength is restricted behind bars.
Because he is sleeping and does not hear them.
Because the visitors are feeding him meat.
Because he is trained to behave politely in front of humans.

subject: English
text: Choose the correct indirect form of: My father said, 'Honesty is the best policy.'
explanation: Universal truths, habitual facts, or geographical facts do not change their tense in reported speech, even if the reporting verb is in the past tense.

options.text: My father said that honesty is the best policy.
My father said that honesty was the best policy.
My father told me that honesty is the best policy.
My father suggested that honesty had been the best policy.

subject: English
text: Where was Ausable's room located in the hotel in 'The Midnight Visitor'?
explanation: Ausable's small room was on the sixth and top floor of a musty, gloomy French hotel.

options.text: On the sixth and top floor
On the ground floor next to the lobby
On the third floor with a balcony view
In the basement of the hotel

subject: English
text: What was Valli's favorite pastime in the story 'Madam Rides the Bus'?
explanation: Valli did not have playmates of her own age, so her favorite pastime was standing in the front doorway of her house and watching the street.

options.text: Standing in the front doorway of her house and watching the street.
Playing with other children in the village playground.
Drawing sketches of buses and passengers.

subject: English
text: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb: Neither the teacher nor the students ________ present.
explanation: When two subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. 'Students' is plural, so the verb must be plural ('were').

subject: English
text: In 'A Question of Trust', how often did Horace Danby commit a robbery, and for what purpose?
explanation: Horace robbed a safe once a year, planning carefully to get enough money to buy rare and expensive books that he loved.

options.text: Once a year; to buy rare and expensive books.
Every month; to pay off his debts.
Once a year; to donate money to an orphanage.
Every week; to buy locks and safe parts.

subject: English
text: In 'The Ball Poem', why does the poet decide not to intrude on the boy or offer him money to buy another ball?
explanation: The poet realizes that money cannot buy back the emotional attachment and memories the boy had with that specific ball; he wants the boy to learn the lesson of loss.

options.text: Because another ball or money is worthless compared to the memories attached to the lost ball.
Because the poet did not have any money with him at that time.
Because the boy was arrogant and would reject the offer.
Because the poet wanted to buy a new ball for himself.

subject: English
text: Which book, gifted by his mother, opened the world of science to Richard Ebright in 'The Making of a Scientist'?
explanation: The children's book 'The Travels of Monarch X' described how monarch butterflies migrate to Central America, sparking Ebright's interest in science.

subject: English
text: Fill in the blank with the appropriate modal verb: You ________ not smoke inside the hospital premises.
explanation: 'Must' is used to express strong obligation or prohibition, which is appropriate for hospital rules.

subject: English
text: In 'The Necklace', how long did it take for Matilda and her husband to pay off the debt incurred for replacing the lost necklace?
explanation: They had to rent a garret, dismiss their servant, and work day and night for ten long years to pay back all their creditors.

subject: English
text: In Chekhov's play 'The Proposal', what physical ailment does Lomov suffer from?
explanation: Lomov is a hypochondriac who suffers from palpitations, a nervous temperament, insomnia, and cold limbs.

subject: English
text: In the poem 'Amanda!', why does Amanda express a desire to be an orphan?
explanation: Amanda wants to escape her mother's constant nagging and restrictions, imagining that an orphan enjoys absolute freedom to roam the streets in silence.

options.text: To escape constant parental nagging and enjoy absolute freedom on the streets.
Because she does not love her parents at all.
To live in a grand orphanage with other kids.
Because she thinks orphans have more money than her.

subject: English
text: What was Bholi's real name, and why was she commonly called 'Bholi' (simpleton) since childhood?
explanation: Her name was Sulekha. When she was ten months old, she fell off her cot, damaging a part of her brain, which made her a slow learner and a simpleton.

options.text: Sulekha; she fell off her cot in infancy, damaging a part of her brain.
Radha; she had smallpox which affected her mental capacity.
Mangla; she was born deaf and could not understand instructions.
Champa; she was neglected by her parents and did not go to school.

subject: English
text: In 'A Baker from Goa', what is the local term for the traditional baker, and what was their unique dress called?
explanation: The traditional baker is called a 'Pader', and they used to wear a peculiar one-piece long frock reaching down to the knees called 'Kabai'.

subject: English
text: Choose the correct indirect form of: The doctor said to him, 'Take medicines regularly.'
explanation: Imperative sentences containing advice change reporting verb 'said to' to 'advised' or 'suggested', and verb takes infinitive 'to' form ('to take').

options.text: The doctor advised him to take medicines regularly.
The doctor ordered him that he should take medicines regularly.
The doctor advised him that he took medicines regularly.
The doctor suggested to him to taking medicines regularly.

subject: English
text: In 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon', what are the names of Belinda's four pets?
explanation: Belinda's pets are Ink (little black kitten), Blink (little gray mouse), Mustard (little yellow dog), and Custard (cowardly dragon).

subject: English
text: In 'The Book That Saved the Earth', who is Noodle, and what is his relation to Think-Tank?
explanation: Noodle is Think-Tank's apprentice/assistant. He is intelligent and tactfully corrects Think-Tank's foolish interpretations without offending him.

options.text: Think-Tank's apprentice who politely and tactfully corrects his mistakes.
The ruler of Mars who orders Think-Tank's space missions.
An Earth spy who infiltrated the Martian spaceship.
Think-Tank's security officer who manages the space force.
